features.text: The patient is a 35-year-old male.
The patient has been experiencing back pain for a while, which has worsened recently.
The back pain radiates down the left leg like an electric toothache.
The patient has difficulty walking or standing for long periods due to back pain.
The patient cannot tie his shoes due to back pain.
The patient uses a cane due to back pain.
The back pain is located in the lower back, radiating through the hip, along the side of the leg, and to the big toe.
The back pain is constant, especially when standing or walking.
The patient rates the back pain as an 8 out of 10, but it can feel like 13 when it is at its worst.
The patient experiences weakness in both legs and his foot drags when walking.
The patient fell off a roof about thirty years ago and may have had a fracture, but no surgery was performed.
The patient has not experienced numbness or tingling in the left leg specifically.
The patient has not experienced bowel or bladder dysfunction.
The patient's primary care physician mentioned an MRI showing a disk issue.
The patient's primary care physician mentioned a disk herniation at the L4-L5 level with nerve root impingement.
The patient's primary care physician mentioned that the disk herniation is causing pain down the leg.
The patient does not remember if spinal stenosis was specifically mentioned in the MRI report.
